chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Hammad, from Abu al-Jaroud, who said:
I heard Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) saying: 'My father narrated to me, from his father (peace be upon him), that the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said:
The habitual drinker of wine is like an idol worshipper.
I said to him, 'And what is the habitual drinker?' He said, 'The one who, whenever he finds it, drinks it.'
ai.seo_question: What is the definition of a habitual wine drinker in Shia hadith and what is their spiritual status?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the spiritual status of the habitual wine drinker by equating them with an idol worshipper, a comparison rooted in the concept of *khamr* (wine) as the 'mother of all intoxicants' that clouds the intellect, the divine trust. The definition of 'habitual' (*mudmin*) is clarified as one who consumes it whenever available, indicating a continuous state of consumption rather than a single instance. This reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on the persistence of the sin and its impact on the soul's purity, linking physical consumption to spiritual deviation.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from Muhammad Bin Isa, from Yunus, from Hammad, from Abu Al Jaroud who said,

‘I heard Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘My<sup>asws</sup> father<sup>asws</sup> narrated to me<sup>asws</sup>, from his<sup>asws</sup> father<sup>asws</sup> that Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘The habitual (drinker of) the wine is like an idol worshipper’.
I said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘And what is the habitual?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The one who, whenever he finds it, drinks it’.
en.sarwar: 1. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from Yunus from Hammad from abu af-Jarud who has said the following: “I once heard abu ‘ Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, saying, ‘My father narrated to me from his father, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, that the Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, has said, ‘A wine addict is like an idol worshipper.’ I (the narrator) then asked, ‘What is a ‘Mudmin’?’ He (the Imam) said, ‘He is one who drinks whenever he finds.’”
